[engine] A probe that must perturb the allocator to read its value has a cost measured in PINS PER GRAPH, not in bytes, and that cost can only be found by experiment. Do not derive the safe budget from tensor dimensions, and do not creep up on the limit: the failure mode is a fail-stop abort at load, not a slowdown.

<!-- generated by harness_engine/build_memories.py from traces/lessons.jsonl -->
<!-- lesson_id: eng-mh-0012 | class: measurement-hygiene | superseded_by: - -->

**class**: `measurement-hygiene`

## 為什麼（because）

CGC_S1_OUT_CAP pins ffn_moe_down with ggml_set_output so a post-synchronize read sees a live buffer. The first version pinned every layer in every graph and both arms died at the load-time warmup decode with kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory -> CGC_METAL_FAIL_STOP abort (2/2), while the control arm without the knob started and decoded at 20.2 t/s in the same session. The obvious explanation -- bytes -- was written into the code comment as '2048 x 6144 x 4B = 50 MB per layer, ~2 GB for 40 layers' and it is WRONG in the direction that matters. Corrected, the boundary is: 40 layers on every graph dies; 11 layers on prefill only ALSO dies; 4 layers on prefill runs; 40 layers on decode runs. At the graph that dies the hook reports ntok=2, so ffn_moe_down is [2048, 8, 2] F32 and eleven pinned layers hold 11 x 131 KB = 1.4 MB. A megabyte and a half does not exhaust a Metal working set, so the controlling variable is the COUNT of tensors marked as graph outputs -- which changes the scheduler's allocation and split -- and it is non-monotone in the phase (prefill chunks are excluded, yet prefill-only pinning is the variant that dies). Two consequences worth keeping: the safe number is empirical (between 4 and 11 here), and a byte budget would have been wrong twice, once as 2 GB and once as 5 MB.

## 反例（counterexample_observed）

Eleven pinned tensors totalling 1.4 MB abort a 16 GB machine's Metal command buffer, while forty pinned tensors on the same tensors abort too -- and forty pinned tensors on a different phase do not.
